title: How to Write a Linear Equation From a Table

scenes.title: How do you turn a table into an equation?
body: Students often see the numbers but miss the rule connecting them.
A linear table gives you two things: slope and starting value.
scenes.narration: If a table gives you x and y values, the question is not just what comes next. The real goal is to find the rule connecting x to y. For a linear table, that rule is built from two things: the slope and the starting value.

scenes.title: First: find the slope
body: Slope means how much y changes for each 1-step change in x.
Here, y goes up by 3 whenever x goes up by 1.
scenes.narration: Slope tells us how fast y changes compared with x. From zero to one, x increases by one and y increases from two to five, which is three. The same thing happens again from one to two. So the slope is three.

scenes.title: Next: find the starting value
body: In y = mx + b, b is the y-value when x = 0.
The table already gives us that row.
scenes.narration: Now we need the starting value. In the form y equals m x plus b, b is the y-value when x equals zero. The table shows that when x is zero, y is two. So b equals two.

scenes.title: Put the pieces into y = mx + b
body: m = 3 is the rate of change.
scenes.narration: Now substitute what each part means. The slope m is three, and the starting value b is two. That gives y equals three x plus two.

scenes.title: The rule is y = 3x + 2
body: Starting value 2 tells us where the rule begins.
scenes.narration: So the equation is y equals three x plus two. The three tells us the rate of change, and the two tells us the starting value. If x equals two, the rule gives eight, which matches the table. That is how the table becomes an equation. The full lesson is available on SUMMIT. Find the complete lesson below.
